newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: GOLF - Campbell allowed to skip golf school.
newsitem.headline: GOLF - Campbell allowed to skip golf school.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Oct 16 - New Zealand golfer Michael Campbell will be playing on the European circuit next year despite not earning enough money to keep his tour card.
Campbell, who was fifth on the European Tour Order of Merit in 1995, finished outside the top 115 this year.
However, he was among the top 150, meaning he is a "category 13" player which enables him to accept unlimited sponsors' invitations to compete in European tournaments.
Campbell, of Wellington, said yesterday that he would not be attending the European tour school in an attempt to regain his tour card.
"I've spoken to Ken Schofield, the tour's chief executive, and he assured me it wouldn't count against me if I play the Australian Open instead of going to the school," Campbell said.
"Had I not earned enough money to be a category 13 player then I would have had no choice, but the fact I play on two tours makes a difference."
Campbell said he was relieved his status had been sorted out and he could now concentrate on preparing for the Australasian circuit.
He will start that campaign at the Dunhill Classic, which he won last year, in Hong Kong on October 30.
Campbell will then play in Morocco before heading for Sydney and the Australian Open which starts on November 21.
Before playing in Hong Kong, Campbell is taking a break after playing eight tournaments in eight weeks.
"I've never done that before and it has taken a lot out of me.
"It's been a difficult year with a lot of doubts in my mind, but I feel things are coming together now."
